name: Grand Hotel Continental
positioning: Grand Hotel Continental Siena, a Starhotels Collezione hotel in the 16th-century Palazzo Gori Pannilini, steps from Piazza del Campo
best_for: Travelers who want a historic palazzo base in central Siena
Wine lovers who want daily tastings in a medieval cellar
Visitors coming for the Palio in July or August

facts.text: The hotel is located just steps from Piazza del Campo and the Duomo in Siena.
The hotel is on Via Banchi di Sopra, the main street known as the Corso Senese, lined with local shops and boutiques.
Once a private palazzo, the building has cotto floors, frescoed ceilings and original chandeliers.
Original frescoes adorn the vaulted ceilings of many of the rooms.
The Salone delle Feste hosts civil ceremonies, wedding receptions and private parties.
The Sapordivino restaurant serves a modern Tuscan menu with fresh pasta, local meats and seasonal specialties.
At Sapordivino, Chef Luca Ciaffarafa offers sophisticated interpretations of classic Sienese dishes.
The Lounge Bar by Sapordivino is in the courtyard of the 16th-century palazzo.
The Heritage Suites have cotto floors, brocade fabrics and gold-leaf details.
The Deluxe View with Terrace room has a private terrace overlooking Siena.
Deluxe View rooms look out over the Basilica di San Domenico and the Duomo.
Craft experiences include decorating a typical Sienese ceramic in a lesson with master artisans.

highlights.text: The wine cellar is hidden inside a subterranean medieval tower, and wine tastings are offered there daily.
The Salone delle Feste ballroom features original trompe-l'oeil frescoes and richly textured marble floors.
In July and August the hotel offers signature experiences for Il Palio, the historic horse race run around Piazza del Campo.
The Panoramic Suite is laid out on two floors, with exposed wood-beamed ceilings and views to the Duomo.
Guests can create their own icon on 24-karat gold, following the techniques of Sienese artists.

considerations.text: Conde Nast Traveler notes this is not a place for high-tech gadgetry or keyless entry; the appeal is antiques and historic character.
The hotel is in Siena's historic centre, set within a 16th-century palazzo rather than a modern building.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing reflecting the hotel's exclusive positioning.
